Photograph: Tony Dejak/AP Ohio Son in custody after Oberlin professor dad and stepmother shot dead in Ohio Daniel Jones held on $3m bail after studio art chair Pipo Nguyen-Duy and Tran Thi Phong found dead at home Auzzy Byrdsell Fri 30 Oct 2026 11.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Oberlin College was shaken on Friday after an award-winning professor of photography who had worked at the Ohio liberal arts college for nearly 30 years was found shot and killed on Wednesday, officials said. Pipo Nguyen-Duy, 64, and his wife, Tran Thi Phong, 56, were found shot to death in their home. The professor’s son, Daniel Jones, 31, was arrested on Wednesday in connection with the deadly shooting. Fifteen-year-old arrested in shooting near Florida university that injured 12 Read more Officials said they were investigating a motive for the killing. Jones was charged with six counts of murder, four counts of felonious assault and one count of tampering with evidence, the authorities said. He was being held on $3m bail after an initial court appearance on Thursday. He did not enter a plea. Nguyen-Duy was the studio art chair at Oberlin College, in north Ohio close to Lake Erie, where officers had responded to a car fire in a parking lot that morning. The investigators found a Toyota hatchback with Oregon license plates registered to Jones. Officers searched his father and stepmother’s home for a wellness check after the arrest. After a forced entry, Nguyen-Duy and Thi Phong were found shot to death, the authorities said. Oberlin police have been in contact with Jones’s mother in Oregon, ABC News reported . Her name was not released, but Oberlin police report she told officials Jones had a mental illness and required medication. Investigators also discovered Jones’s wallet and passport along with ammunition in the car before finding Jones about a mile away more than an hour later, the police said. The officers responded to a call from a resident reporting a “wet, disheveled man” at her front door and the authorities took him into custody without incident. Officials said Jones had cuts to his face and injuries to his hand and arm at the time of the arrest. His lawyer, Jenifer Berki Merrill, said he preferred to go by his birth name, Asia Nguyen-Duy. Pipo Nguyen-Duy migrated to the US from Vietnam in 1975 as a political refugee. He was considered highly respected at Oberlin College and had been honored for his photography and been named a Guggenheim fellow. Photograph: Hertfordshire Constabulary/PA UK news Family of Watford woman set alight ‘desperate for answers’ after attack Appeal for information comes after Brenda Raymond, 80, was set on fire outside her flat on Monday Raphael Boyd Sat 14 Nov 2026 12.59 EST Last modified on Sat 14 Nov 2026 14.39 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The family of an elderly woman who was set on fire outside a block of flats in Watford have said they are “desperate for answers”. Brenda Raymond, 80, was found set alight outside her flat on Caractacus Cottage View on Monday. She was taken to a nearby hospital, where she is in critical condition. Hertfordshire constabulary have said a 33-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit arson with intent to endanger life but has been released on bail with strict conditions. Raymond’s family said the attack had left them in “complete shock” and that they were confused over why she was targeted. In a statement issued via Hertfordshire constabulary, they said: “Words cannot describe how distressing the past few days have been for us as a family. “Our beautiful, chatty, fun-loving and much-loved Brenda, who loves to keep fit and dancing, has suffered catastrophic injuries in the most devastating of circumstances; circumstances which have left us all in complete shock. “We simply cannot understand why anyone would have wanted to hurt her in this way. Someone out there knows something. They know what happened to Brenda. We are desperate for answers and are pleading for anyone with information to please come forward.” The family also asked for their privacy to be respected during this “unimaginably difficult time”. Police believe that Raymond was attacked as she returned home at around noon, with her attackers pouring some kind of flammable liquid on her before setting her alight. Detectives said that an accelerant was also poured through the letterbox of a nearby flat, but they have not officially linked the two events. The decision to publicly name Raymond was made by police with the blessing of her family on Wednesday in the hope it would lead to anyone with knowledge of the attack coming forward. DI Adam Bridges, from the major crime unit, said: “This was an appalling and deeply distressing attack on an elderly woman who suffered horrific injuries after being set alight outside her own home. “Our thoughts very much remain with Brenda and her family as we continue to do everything we can to find out what happened and who is responsible. “Her family are understandably distraught and have taken the step of releasing her name and photograph to help jog people’s memories around this distressing and highly unusual incident. “Someone out there knows something. You may have witnessed suspicious activity, heard a conversation, noticed unusual behaviour, or captured something on CCTV or dashcam footage without realising its significance. “Please do not assume that what you know is too small or unimportant to tell us about. It could be a seemingly insignificant piece of information that provides investigators with the breakthrough they need. “If you know anything about what happened to Brenda or think you may have information that could assist our inquiries, please come forward. Your information could be crucial in helping us find answers and bring those responsible to justice.” Explore more on these topics UK news news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland
